news.title: Atlas Robot’s New Hand May Outperform Humanlike Designs
paras: Robots need a hand that can pick, move, and grip objects easily to help them work in real life. Building such a hand is very hard because it must be strong, flexible, and simple to make. Boston Dynamics says their new robot hand should have three fingers and one thumb.

The hand needs 13 degrees of freedom, meaning 13 movable joints. These joints let the robot grasp objects in many ways, just like a human hand. Because of this design, the robot can pick delicate items without crushing them, making it safer for people.

news.title: Intel gets waiver after worries fuzzy US ban on foreign-made robots may hit fabs
paras: 26 The interior of Intel's chip manufacturing facility named Fab 52 in Chandler, Arizona. The uncertainty surrounding the Federal Communications Commission ban on certain foreign-made robots was revealed in the agency’s decision to grant Intel’s waiver request.

On October 22, the FCC published its order allowing Intel to continue using the foreign-made robots in US semiconductor manufacturing facilities for a period of one year. The robots in question are automated guided vehicles operating on “tracks or predefined paths” while often requiring operator oversight, according to Intel’s website. They help to move materials and items around within warehouses and factory floors.

news.title: Is Taekwondo an art or A Sport?
paras: And then… silence, and then someone from the crowd shouted… “Is Taekwondo a sport or is it a performing arts?” Well we are here to answer that question! Did you know that Taekwondo is Korean? In Korean, chung and hung mean blue and red.

They use these colours to represent a competitor at a competition. You wear protective gear in that colour on your stomach. Otherwise, you wear your own white gear. According to sources such as The Korea Herald and Kiddle, Taekwondo is a form of performing art, because you don’t just fight, you learn a pattern.

news.title: Zoo animals enjoy spooktacular Halloween treats
paras: Animals at Whipsnade Zoo are enjoying an early taste of Halloween with some special treats. The lemurs and macaques tucked into carved pumpkins to find sweetcorn and peppers, whilst rhino Hugo enjoyed his usual breakfast of hay and cabbage.

The zoo's keepers been trying to find creative ways to encourage the animals' natural instincts to hunt and explore. Matthew Webb, Head of Zoological Operations at Whipsnade Zoo, said: "As everyone counts down to Halloween, our zookeepers used seasonal squashes to make sure the animals don't miss out on any of the fun"

sport.title: Daniil Medvedev uses Novak Djokovic example to explain how tennis has changed since he arrived on the ATP Tour
paras: Daniil Medvedev has seen men’s tennis change a lot since he first arrived on the ATP Tour. Medvedev has been on the ATP Tour since 2016, when he was 20 years old, and since then has become one of the best players in men’s tennis.

During his emergence to the very top of the ATP rankings, Novak Djokovic has been a consistent force, even now at 39 years old. Medvedev has now explained how he has noticed tennis change during the last 10 years, making a comment about Djokovic. How would you feel if Novak Djokovic got a wildcard to the ATP Finals?

sport.title: How much prize money Emma Raducanu has won in her tennis career since her US Open title in 2021
paras: Emma Raducanu is one of tennis’ most famous faces, but this year, she has not been quite so visible. After all, despite arguably enjoying her most successful season since winning the US Open , it has been a campaign laden with illness and injury turmoil.

It has now been over four months since we last saw her play a competitive match; her 2026 campaign is surely over , but she is yet to properly confirm it. Despite this, the British superstar remains a hugely recognisable individual with a brand that arguably has evolved beyond tennis now.

sport.title: ‘Staying healthy is a real skill’: Mouratoglou explains why Zverev deserves to be No. 1
paras: Patrick Mouratoglou believes Alexander Zverev fully deserves his No. 1 ranking, even if Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz are better players.

Staying healthy, he argues, is “a real skill” that demands sacrifice, and Zverev’s two Grand Slam titles in 2026 marked a mental breakthrough. Alexander Zverev may not be the best player in the world, but his ranking is fully deserved. That is Patrick Mouratoglou’s view, set out in a video on his social media channels in which he argued that staying healthy is a skill in itself, and part of a player’s value.

sport.title: Roger Federer shares the advice he had given Alexander Zverev for years before he won his first Grand Slam tit
paras: When Roger Federer retired, and Rafael Nadal followed suit just two years later, it felt like the end of an era. Novak Djokovic was still present on the ATP Tour, but two of his greatest rivals had finally been removed.

Now, only the Serbian was left to uphold the dominance that three men had established over the sport for two decades. Therefore, it was expected that, at last, an entire generation would finally get their chance to challenge for Grand Slams. The likes of Daniil Medvedev, Stefanos Tsitsipas and even Casper Ruud were backed to be the biggest beneficiaries, with Alexander Zverev chief among them.

sport.title: Taylor Fritz Boosts ATP Finals Qualification Hopes With Victory Over Paul, Cobolli Denied
paras: Taylor Fritz overcame Tommy Paul to reach the Lyon final while Flavio Cobolli missed out on a place in the final. The American boosted his chances of reaching the Nitto ATP Finals after defeating Tommy Paul 6-3 7-5. It was a good display from Paul in what was a high-quality semi-final as Fritz boosted his chances of making Turin.
After the win Fritz admitted it was a high level match, “We know each other’s games so well. Since we’ve gone pro, we’ve always gone back and forth. No one’s ever won two matches in a row.
